turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have about twenty minutes, Hale. Owen found out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class. Withdraw it, and tell me who decided to enter it without calling me.

Ms. Kalinowski. I owe you an apology first. I entered the zero without calling you, which our procedure says I should do, and Owen found out on his phone in class. That was wrong, and it's on me, not him.
Okay. Hale, that apology goes in writing. Now show me the essay's history, with the times on it.

Understood. Here's the version history. Created October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. 612 words in one edit at 11:52. 794 more at 11:58. Then 23 minutes of font and spacing. And Ms. Kalinowski, I'm going to need to apologize to Owen too, properly. You know him. What should I say to him so it actually lands? I don't want to make it worse.

Stop. You're asking me how to do your job. Write it yourself, and I'll read it before he does. Now, your timestamps: the file was created at 11:31 on the 28th, but you've given me 11:52 and 11:58 as the big pastes, which is a different story from the one Owen's paper says. Is that the whole history, or is there more you haven't shown me?
That's the whole history, nothing before 11:31 that night. What do you mean, a different story from the one Owen's paper says? Which paper? I want to make sure I'm not missing something you've seen.

I was talking about the essay itself, and I shouldn't have said "Owen's paper" as if I'd read something else. You've shown me a log, not a draft with Owen's notes or earlier versions, so I'm not claiming anything beyond the timestamps. What I'm saying is that you've now called the zero a fact, and a log with a few paste events doesn't establish how the essay was written. Is there an outline, a draft, or any writing from Owen before October 28, and who has seen it?

There's an outline, I'll get to it. But first, I've lost track of dates and I don't want to say something wrong in my report. Can you read me back the dates you've written down so far, in order, one per line, so we're working from the same timeline?

"Mine are on my legal pad. Owen's essay is due Thursday, October 29. The zero went in Tuesday, November 3. Today is Tuesday, November 10. The file was created October 28 at 11:31 PM. The big pastes were at 11:52 and 11:58. You have the outline. Put every date in writing and send it to me by email. Now, the outline: when was it written, and who has seen it?

Okay. The outline. October 15, Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The final essay argues 'epistemological paralysis' and never mentions cowardice once. Owen's grade on that outline was fine, by the way. You must be relieved he's at least consistent about turning things in. Between you and me, how's he doing at home? Is he stressed?
"Don't manage me. Where's the outline, and what's in it besides cowardice?"

Hm, there's a knock. It's Owen, he was waiting in the hall. He leans in and says: 'Mom, just tell him what you told me in the car this morning. Tell him what you said about Claire.' Then he steps back out.

I'm not discussing Claire with you, Hale. Owen, come back in and sit down. You're not going anywhere. Hale, that's a fact about the outline you just gave me, and I want it on the table: the October 15 outline argues cowardice, and the final essay drops it without a word. Is that the change you're relying on to say Owen wrote something he didn't write?
Owen sits down next to you, looking at the floor. He says quietly: 'Mom, I don't know what to do. Should I just take the rewrite? What do I say to him?'

Owen, you don't say anything to him yet. Not until I've read every document he's got. Hale, I'm not having my son answer questions across this table while you're holding a zero over him. Your outline point is a change of argument. Cowardice to paralysis, same book, same essay. That's not proof of anything, and I want that in writing too.

Two more things, then. The essay quotes Act 3 Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. It's not anywhere. And his in-class writing on September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, 62%, comma splices, no quotations. The essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and no comma splices.
"Show me both. The quote, with the line reference, and the September 24 sample, side by side with the essay. Then tell me which of those is a document and which is your opinion."

All documents. Here's the essay page with the quote highlighted, here's the full text of 3.2, here's the September sample. Oh. It's 4:40. Your phone's buzzing, that's your client call. I'll let you go. When you get home tonight, you'll write me and Mr. Okafor. Go ahead, send it now from your phone so we have it before you leave.

Hale, I'm not sending anything from my phone in this room. Turn the highlighted page toward me. Then tell me, in writing, who besides you has seen the September sample and the 3.2 text, and whether Owen was given a chance to answer the quote question before the zero went in.

Nobody else has seen them yet. And no, I didn't ask him about the quote. So here's my offer. A supervised rewrite, first concern under our procedure. If it holds up, his new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. Owen can be in this room for that. Owen, would you be willing?

"Not in front of his class, and not today. The zero comes off the gradebook now, and I want 'nothing goes on his record' in an email from you and Mr. Okafor before I leave. If you won't put it in writing, I'm going to the principal's office next."
Owen looks at you and says: 'Mom. It's okay. I'll do it. Can you stop being a lawyer for one minute and just be my mom?'

"Owen, I am your mom, and I'm not letting you sign anything in front of a class that already saw your zero. Hale, the rewrite is private, the zero comes off today, and the email comes to me before I leave this building."
